descs: The moor rolls on, heather and stone, gray under a wide sky.

spots.name: Windbreak Stones
spots.desc: A ring of stones worn to stumps by wind that never fully stops. Nothing grows in their lee but a paler kind of moss. East, the ground climbs toward the moor's last cairn.

spots.name: The Long Sight
spots.desc: High, open ground. On a clear day you can see the whole moor from here, and the mountains beyond it hard and white. Today is not quite a clear day.

spots.name: The Last Cairn
spots.desc: A cairn taller than the rest, stones added by hands that never explained why. North the ground turns rough, unmarked, toward wherever it is the old oath was sworn.
spots.brief: The last cairn. Rough ground north.

spots.name: Cloudfoot
spots.desc: Mist pools low here even at noon, thick enough to lose a boot-print in three strides. West the ground rises toward a tall cairn just visible through the murk.

spots.name: Cairnwatch
spots.desc: A line of boundary cairns marches south, older than any border they were meant to keep. West the ground falls away toward smoke on the horizon — the Iron Downs, by the color of it.

spots.name: Tower Rise
spots.desc: A shoulder of higher ground, and on it a signal tower gone to ruin, roofless, its stair still climbing into the wet air. Sergeant Rook's dark beacon, if the rumor's true, stands south of here.

spots.name: Peat Score
spots.desc: Black trenches, cut and abandoned, half-flooded now and smelling of old smoke that was never lit. A plank walkway, rotten in the middle, threads between them.

spots.name: Boot-Track Hollow
spots.desc: A shallow dip where the heather's beaten flat in a line, boot-tracks going in step and stopping nowhere in particular. Whoever left them is still walking, somewhere close.

spots.name: Mistfall
spots.desc: The mist sits so thick in this hollow it beads on your sleeves. Sound carries strangely — footsteps that are not yours, and then are not there at all.

spots.name: The Elbow
spots.desc: The moor's edge bends hard here, heather giving way to wetter, softer ground east. Hollowbrook's low country starts somewhere past the haze.

spots.name: Beacon Hill
spots.desc: A squat stone hill with an iron cresset at its crown, cold and rust-streaked. Whoever last tended it left the ladder in place, at least. East, a rough track runs toward the drovers' waystation.
spots.brief: The cold beacon on its hill.

actions.label: climb up and light the beacon (grace)
fx: The old brushwood catches on the third try, and flame climbs the cresset for the first time in a decade. It will be seen from the wall.
The ladder holds, the kindling doesn't. Too damp through to catch. It can be tried again.

actions.label: judge the beacon properly (wits)
fx: The cresset's rusted through at the base — light it and it comes down with whoever's standing under it. Worth telling Sergeant Rook plainly.
Rust and rot, but you can't be certain past that without climbing it yourself.

actions.label: force the rusted cresset alight (might)
fx: You don't wait on the wind or the damp. You wrench the ladder true, wedge the kindling home by hand, and make the old iron take a flame it hasn't held in a decade.
The ladder groans and the kindling scatters. Whatever this needs, brute handling isn't helping it.

actions.label: climb it on nerve alone (will)
fx: You don't stop to weigh the rust. You climb before your nerve can talk you out of it, and get the flame going before doubt catches up with you.
Halfway up, your nerve goes first and your grip second. You're back on solid ground, no closer to a flame.

variants.brief: The beacon hill. Char still marks the cresset's rim.

spots.name: The Waystation Track
spots.desc: Wagon-ruts converge here, deep enough to twist an ankle in the dark. A waystation stands north, its palisade patched with whatever driftwood the moor gives up.

spots.name: Twin Ruts
spots.desc: The drovers' road runs straight here for once, two deep ruts worn by centuries of cattle and coin both heading the same way south, toward Highward's market.

spots.name: Sedge Flat
spots.desc: Coarse sedge grass, ankle-deep water hiding under most of it. Something has been through recently, flattening a path east that doesn't look like a drover's doing.
spots.brief: Wet sedge, a strange path east.

spots.name: The Hut Path
spots.desc: A worn footpath, too narrow for a cart, climbing toward a squat turf-roofed hut just visible through the heather. Smoke rises from it, thin but steady.
spots.brief: A footpath to a turf hut.

spots.name: Cliff Edge
spots.desc: The moor drops away here, a long scree slope down toward Hollowbrook's wetter ground. Cairns line the drop, warning rather than marking.

spots.name: Old Sheepfold
spots.desc: A drystone fold, roofless, its gate long since rotted off its hinge. Wool catches on the stones still, though no flock has passed through in years.

spots.name: Drover's Rest
spots.desc: A flat stone worn smooth as a bench, cold ash banked beside it from a hundred fires. Someone dropped a tally-stick here and never came back for it.

spots.name: The Cairn Field
spots.desc: Dozens of small cairns, close-set, older than the Watch that now claims this ground. One, larger than the rest, has been opened at some point and never quite closed again.

spots.name: Wet Hollow
spots.desc: Standing black water, reeds at its edge, and a smell of iron that has nothing to do with Cinderhall. South the last shielings mark the moor's edge before Highward.

spots.name: Standing Stone
spots.desc: A single worked stone, taller than a man, its carving worn past reading by weather that has had four centuries to try. It faces north, toward the last cairn, and nothing else.

spots.name: The Grey Ford
spots.desc: A shallow crossing, stones slick underfoot, water the color the moor gives everything eventually. East the ground softens toward Hollowbrook's dike country.

spots.name: West Shieling
spots.desc: A herder's summer hut, empty and shuttered, close enough to Highward's wall to hear the changing of the watch-horn. West the road to the armoury cuts off toward the Iron Downs.

spots.name: The Moor Road
spots.desc: Where the heather gives out and a beaten track drops south toward Highward's wall, close enough that the watch-horn carries. North the moor opens out, wide and gray, cairn after cairn.

spots.name: The Watch Cairn
spots.desc: A cairn built by the Watch itself, recent by moor standards, marking the edge of ground they still bother to patrol. Highward's wall shows gray through the haze south.

spots.name: East Shieling
spots.desc: A second summer hut, its roof half fallen in. East the road to the barracks cuts off toward Hollowbrook's dikes.

onEnter: The mist thickens, and boots fall into step behind you — in time, unhurried, and not yours.

vars.NAME: the Ruined Signal Tower
vars.VIEW: the whole moor spreads gray in every direction, and Coldpass is a white line north

wm_drovers_stick.name: a drover's tally-stick
wm_drovers_stick.hint: notches for every head of cattle a drover never came back to collect on

wm_lost_sentry.name: the Lost Sentry
wm_lost_sentry.desc: Watch-gray gone the color of the mist itself, still marching a patrol route that stopped mattering centuries ago.
onDeath: The Lost Sentry breaks step at last and comes apart into old wool and colder air. Whatever round it was walking, it has finally finished.
